tasks.short: Recommend personnel actions for maintenance workers

steps.what: Assess personnel circumstances and hear the worker's account
Recommend hires, promotions, transfers, discharges or disciplinary measures to the authorised manager

tasks.design: Keep the supervisor's assessment and recommendation human. Use the existing {HCM} case record and {DOCS} policy without introducing worker scoring or an automated personnel decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: The facts and fair treatment cannot be reduced to maintenance output metrics.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can support discussion; they do not replace it.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting accounts, proportionality and effects on the worker.
tasks.human_edge: Hear context, challenge assumptions and take responsibility for a recommendation.
tasks.altitude: Decision rights and weekly personnel work stay the same.

reach.task: Check the process for a proposed disciplinary action
reach.learn: Employment policy and the limits of supervisory authority

evidence.claim: Personnel recommendations require contextual assessment and discussion; this design does not automate them.

assumptions: Boundary ends with a recommendation, before the authorised manager's decision and any employment change; their unchanged work is outside this task.
The supervisor reads existing records and gathers the worker's account in s1; no structured score, machine action or free input capture is assumed.
Check native case access before adding software; none is proposed here.
Zero incremental upkeep because there is no new automation, data feed, template or scoring policy.
research_questions: Does the current recommendation process provide enough time to hear the worker?

already_counted.description: Assess the case and write the recommendation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net zero. The recommendation and discussion remain intact; no personnel administration saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate accidents and prepare findings reports

steps.what: Investigate accidents or injuries and preserve observations and witness accounts
Prepare accident reports from the evidence packet
Check evidence, distinguish causes from hypotheses, and release findings reports

tasks.design: Configure a report form in {DOCS} to reuse the incident header and organise evidence references. The supervisor writes conclusions, checks the final report against original accounts and releases it to the safety adviser.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report formatting competes with field investigation, but causal conclusions remain contextual.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields and reusable report sections can avoid repeated header entry.
tasks.still_hard: Preserving conflicting accounts and distinguishing an observed fact from a possible cause.
tasks.human_edge: Conduct a fair investigation and decide what the evidence supports.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less report assembly; investigative responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.task: Track a corrective action to verified completion

evidence.claim: A native document form can reuse incident header fields while people write and check causal findings.

assumptions: Boundary covers the supervisor's investigation and internal report, not emergency response, medical care, regulatory submission or corrective maintenance.

Supervisor produces incident id, time, location, asset id if known, observation text and evidence references in s1; all capture and witness discussion remain in its 55 hours. Unknown fields stay unknown, and a manual report is the fallback.
s2 retains 17.5 hours for narrative composition and evidence assembly. No model infers injury severity, blame or root cause.
Test native document forms before custom code; existing storage runtime earns no labour saving.
s3 approval binds the completed report; later edits require another review.
research_questions: How much report time is header and evidence-reference repetition rather than investigation or reasoning?

already_counted.description: Capture evidence, compose findings and review the report

incremental.description: Maintain the report form and check broken evidence references

approvals.approved_version: Completed report revision with evidence references and findings; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+17.5+20=92.5; gross 7.5 minus upkeep 1 gives net 6.5. E1 scenario assumes reusable headers save 30% of report preparation; manual reports and complex investigations can absorb all of that gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct or arrange maintenance and safety training

steps.what: Identify worker training needs and choose safe instruction and equipment
Arrange training dates, places and worker invitations
Conduct safety, repair and maintenance training and observe practical competence

tasks.design: Use {LMS} enrolment and {CALENDAR} invitations to arrange the supervisor's chosen session. The supervisor checks the arrangement before sending it and still teaches, demonstrates and observes competence in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordinating the session is separable from safe practical teaching.
tasks.enabler_now: Native enrolment and calendar features can reuse an explicit session plan.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding when a worker can perform a hazardous technique safely.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt demonstrations to the worker and intervene during unsafe practice.
tasks.altitude: Less scheduling effort; no additional authority to certify competence.

reach.task: Resolve conflicts in a practical training calendar
reach.learn: Session capacity, prerequisites and equipment availability

evidence.claim: Learning-system enrolment and calendar invitations can support training coordination; practical competence still requires human observation.

assumptions: Boundary is the supervisor's planning, arranging and delivery time; learner attendance and any external instructor's unchanged preparation are outside the denominator.

Supervisor captures worker ids, course or technique, instructor, equipment, duration and proposed date in s1. In s2 the supervisor checks availability, capacity and recipients, handles conflicts and confirms the final arrangement; that input work is in its retained 7.5 hours.
No machine infers qualifications or safe staffing from calendar availability. Missing prerequisites or calendar access means manual scheduling.
Test native enrolment before integration; invitation runtime is not human time.
Hands-on training and competence observation retain all 65 baseline hours.
unknowns: Proportion of training arranged with outside instructors
research_questions: Do native enrolment invitations reduce coordinator effort without increasing scheduling conflicts?

already_counted.description: Plan training, handle scheduling exceptions and deliver instruction

incremental.description: Maintain session mappings and resolve invitation configuration issues

approvals.approved_version: Final session id, date, duration, venue, instructor and recipients; edits void confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+7.5+65=92.5; gross 7.5 less upkeep 1 gives net 6.5. E1 scenario halves scheduling time only; irregular outside sessions may leave no net saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop, implement and evaluate maintenance procedures

steps.what: Evaluate maintenance performance, hazards and current policies with technicians
Develop maintenance policies and procedures from the change brief
Walk through draft procedures and authorise the exact release version
Implement maintenance procedures and evaluate their use on the equipment

tasks.design: Use controlled sections in {DOCS} to assemble a maintenance procedure from the supervisor's change brief. Keep technical writing, equipment walk-through and release decisions with the supervisor, and use {OPS_SYSTEM} for existing maintenance records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures combine repeated document structure with equipment-specific safety reasoning.
tasks.enabler_now: Native versioning and reusable sections can reduce assembly without generating technical instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the proposed procedure is safe, usable and suitable for the actual asset.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile technician experience with instructions and verify the procedure at the equipment.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated document assembly; maintenance strategy and implementation responsibility stay human.

reach.task: Test the practical sequence of a revised maintenance instruction
reach.learn: Equipment limitations and safe verification methods

evidence.claim: IFS Ultimo supports maintenance strategies, technician downtime reporting and links to enterprise systems; this supports the existing maintenance-record context, not automatic procedure authorship.
Controlled document sections can reduce repeated procedure assembly while a supervisor retains technical judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisory policy development and implementation evaluation, not technicians' execution of maintenance work. Overlapping training effort must be allocated once in a roll-up.

Supervisor produces asset applicability, change reason, source instruction revisions and selected existing sections in s1, retaining all 25 hours. s2 includes selection checks and all new technical prose in 17.5 retained hours; no free structured change packet is assumed.
Existing approved sections have an identified document owner and revision; unavailable or mismatched material is written manually. Any new section curation is in incremental upkeep.
Test native document reuse and versioning first. Machine runtime and existing asset data feeds earn no saving.
Release approval concerns the written procedure only; implementation remains supervised and subject to existing local safety controls.
unknowns: Who is authorised to release equipment-specific procedures
research_questions: Which procedure sections can be reused without changing technical meaning or applicability?

already_counted.description: Evaluate evidence, write technical changes, review and supervise implementation

incremental.description: Maintain controlled section revisions and remove obsolete reusable text

approvals.approved_version: Final procedure revision including asset scope, instructions and references; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+17.5+20+30=92.5; gross 7.5 less upkeep 1.5 gives net 6. E1 scenario saves 30% of document assembly only; novel assets and unreusable safety instructions can erase the saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The supervisor keeps personnel, incident and safety decisions while spending less time on repeated documents and invitations.
reach: Help the safety adviser verify corrective-action closure
Help the learning coordinator resolve practical-session conflicts
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who tests procedures with technicians and spends the recovered coordination time on practical coaching.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
